final.memo:
The Company presents a compelling opportunity to capture value in a business that is fundamentally mispriced due to a crowded, sensationalist short campaign. While the market is fixated on allegations regarding the legality of the distributor model, it has ignored a machine that generated $418.9 million in free cash flow in 2011 [D02, D05].

Based on a post-event earnings power of $3.88 per share and applying a normalized peer multiple of 15.8x, we believe the business is worth $61.50 per share [D03, D04, D06]. This valuation offers a substantial margin of safety, with a hard floor of $27.50 supported by net cash and distressed earnings power [D04].

We believe the market has it wrong because it is pricing the company as a binary regulatory failure rather than a durable, high-margin consumer business [D05, D06]. Our analysis suggests the 16.3% operating margins are indicative of a sustainable retail engine that will continue to generate cash despite public debates [D02, D06].

Our plan is to let the operational results do the heavy lifting; no activist intervention is required to unlock this value [D02, D05]. We expect the market to reconcile the company's strong cash generation over the next four quarters, prompting a short-squeeze as bearish positions are covered [D02, D05].

The primary risk remains potential regulatory overreach, which we view as the sole catalyst for an immediate exit [D07]. Barring formal enforcement action, we are content to hold as the market re-rates the stock toward its intrinsic value [D01, D07].

We are initiating a 5% position in the common stock to capitalize on the current dislocation. We will size this to conviction, maintaining liquidity to exit within five days should the regulatory thesis break [D04, D05].
